# Constraint Systems Institute: foundational source-access guide

> Attributed formalism, glossary and dependency reading aid. The exact PDFs are authoritative. This is neither a full manuscript conversion nor an independent proof audit.

## Current catalogue updates

The six curated foundational summaries below retain their exact source editions. In particular, the May Metricity summary is historical and does not summarize the October revision. Current catalogue updates are separate PDF editions; their publication and checksum records are in [the edition registry](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/data/repository-editions.json). Existing consumer evidence and frozen imports are not rebound.

## Coverage and source hierarchy

The current canonical catalogue has 213 work records, derived from [papers.json](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers.json). This guide covers only the 6 verified foundational reading editions in [the public source registry](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/registry.json). It does not ingest or summarize all catalogue manuscripts. Existing source holds and author exclusions remain outside this expansion.

For theorem statements, equations, hypotheses, proofs and bibliography, read the exact versioned PDF. Use an exact release DOI plus its SHA256 identity when identifying text. An all-versions work DOI is for discovery. A preferred reading edition is not automatically the frozen edition imported by a consumer. Cover dates and publisher release dates are separately recorded below.

## Foundational direction and reading order

The Kernel manuscript argues from actual non-degenerate determinate construction and original incidence to necessary Admissibility, Standing, Reference and Irreversibility roles. These are incurred objecthood commitments, not an optional explanatory overlay. Evidence: [kernel: Proposition 2.4, PDF pp. 14-17; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=14); [kernel: Theorem 2.8 / Corollary 2.9, PDF pp. 20-21; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=20); [kernel: Theorem 3.1 / Theorem 3.6, PDF pp. 24-27; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=24). These are attributed manuscript claims.

Editorial reading path: [Non-Degenerate Construction and the Kernel of Admissibility](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/summary.md) -> [The AMetric Boundary as a Unique Regime-Invariant Constraint on Admissibility-Bearing Construction](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/summary.md) -> [The Structure of Admissibility](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/summary.md) -> [A Fixed-Domain Exhaustion Theorem](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/summary.md) -> [Anchor, Tensor, and Skin](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/summary.md). [Metricity as Licensed Description](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/summary.md) is the physical metric-licensing branch. The consumer's stated one-way support order is recorded in [ats: Section 1.4, PDF p. 3; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875011](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf#page=3); this guide's use of preferred reading editions does not resolve the older reference identities named there.

## How to distinguish relationships

- **Logical dependency:** a consumer uses a warranted premise or construction under stated conditions. A bibliography entry alone establishes only named support. Local reconstruction/reproof is recorded separately.
- **Projection:** an internal prerequisite relation on the same declared background. Metricity Definition 2.12 defines a dependency order, not temporal emergence; Definition 5.2 uses local minimality. Evidence: [metricity: Definition 2.12, PDF p. 9; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=9); [metricity: Definition 5.2, PDF p. 15; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=15).
- **Certificate assembly:** warrants and preservation conditions are combined on the declared original domain; execution requires its own occurrence conditions. Evidence: [ats: Theorem 7.3 / Theorem 7.5, PDF pp. 22-24; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875011](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf#page=22).
- **Reading order:** an editorial sequence for understanding the work. It is not a verified theorem-import edge and does not license substituting editions.

## Working glossary

These scoped paraphrases do not replace the manuscripts' definitions.

- **Admissibility:** Bivalent qualification of the fixed original question. An admissibility bit is an exact description only if every required original observation is constant on its fibres. Evidence: [structure: Theorems 5.5-5.6, PDF pp. 16-17; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22874934](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/manuscript.pdf#page=16).

- **Standing:** Warrant to bear the relevant role or target interpretation. A formal or calculational interpretation does not by itself supply physical standing. Evidence: [metricity: Definitions 2.7-2.11, PDF pp. 8-9; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=8).

- **Reference:** Preservation of the already identified subject and original incidence through representation and reuse; a different occurrence is not automatically evidence for the original claim. Evidence: [kernel: Proposition 2.4; Theorem 2.8 / Corollary 2.9, PDF pp. 14-21; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=14).

- **Irreversibility:** Retention of original qualification and constraint history. Retaining a failure history is distinct from forcing every later endpoint to remain negative; the latter needs an additional edge condition. Evidence: [structure: Theorems 6.3-6.6, PDF pp. 20-21; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22874934](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/manuscript.pdf#page=20).

- **Complete profile:** The context and all required semantic coordinates on the declared original domain. It is richer than a qualification bit and need not identify a unique occupant. Evidence: [exhaustion: Section 3 / Theorem 3.3; Theorem 8.1 / Corollary 8.2, PDF pp. 9-27; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875070](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/manuscript.pdf#page=9).

- **Admissible interior:** The greatest safe continuation region for fixed, independently supplied qualification and edge data. It may be empty; uniqueness of the greatest region does not mean uniqueness of every safe subset or of a physical occupant. Evidence: [structure: Theorems 6.3-6.6, PDF pp. 20-21; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22874934](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/manuscript.pdf#page=20).

- **AMetric boundary:** At the fixed authoritative equality-only atom interface, invariant readouts cannot supply additional original-incidence warrant without warranted richer input. Equality-based formal structures and independently warranted enrichment remain possible. Evidence: [ametric: Proposition 3.8; Theorem 7.5 / Section 7.6, PDF pp. 21-40; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22848051](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=21).

- **L-metric:** The locally minimal projection interface for warranted physical metric description on the declared background. Its order is a dependency order, not a temporal sequence; licensing generates neither metric structure nor standing nor ontology. Evidence: [metricity: Definition 2.12; Definition 5.2; Theorem 6.2 / Corollary 6.3, PDF pp. 9-17; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=9).

- **Anchor / Tensor / Skin (ATS):** Context / complete semantic content / identity-preserving realization in the fixed-domain decomposition. Tensor here is a semantic role and should not be assumed to mean a physical tensor field. Evidence: [ats: Section 2.4; Theorems 3.1-3.3; Section 3.4, PDF pp. 6-8; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875011](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf#page=6).

- **Certificate assembly:** Combining the stated primitive warrants, original-question coverage and compatible retained input/output conditions. Joint original-domain factorization is required for sequential substitution; a licence does not supply an executed occurrence. Evidence: [ats: Theorem 7.3; Theorem 7.5, PDF pp. 22-24; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875011](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf#page=22).

- **Work DOI / exact release DOI:** all-versions discovery identity / one particular publisher release. Use the registry fields separately; neither chronology nor a matching title alone confirms the bytes imported by a consumer.

## AMetric and physical metric licensing limits

The equality-only authority condition is specific to the fixed original boundary problem. It does not erase formal symbols, equality patterns, tuple relations or all calculational distinctions. AMetric Proposition 3.8 allows invariant formal structures, including equality-based discrete metrics. Theorem 7.5 accommodates independently warranted richer input. Evidence: [ametric: Section 3.1 / Proposition 3.3 / Definition 3.4, PDF pp. 17-19; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22848051](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=17); [ametric: Proposition 3.8, PDF pp. 21-22; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22848051](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=21); [ametric: Theorem 7.5 / Section 7.6, PDF pp. 39-40; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22848051](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=39).

Metricity's weak formal/model/calculational interpretation can precede strong physical interpretation and standing. Its conditional licensing theorem does not construct metric structure, standing or ontology. Evidence: [metricity: Definitions 2.7-2.11, PDF pp. 8-9; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=8); [metricity: Theorem 6.2 / Corollary 6.3, PDF pp. 16-17; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=16). No globally unique metric interface is asserted across all backgrounds; see [metricity: Definition 2.12, PDF p. 9; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=9).

## Six exact reading editions

The following summaries retain their exact source editions, including historical editions where the catalogue now has a newer preferred PDF. Their evidence links refer to these exact reading PDFs, not to an unconfirmed older producer edition named by another paper.

### Non-Degenerate Construction and the Kernel of Admissibility

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/non-degenerate-construction-and-the-kernel-of-admissibility-10-5281-zenodo-19324199/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22968658) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19324199)

Edition: Reference edition; manuscript cover 2026-09-26; publisher release 2026-09-25; 73 PDF pages; 659394 bytes. SHA256: `4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. Non-Degenerate Construction and the Kernel of Admissibility: An Exhaustion Theorem for Standing, Reference, and Irreversibility. Reference edition, 2026-09-26. SHA256 4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22968658.

#### Imports

Begins with non-degenerate determinate construction and original incidence. It does not assume the downstream binary interface, occupancy or ATS decomposition as premises.

#### Establishes

The manuscript derives necessary Admissibility, Standing, Reference and Irreversibility roles from incurred objecthood obligations, and proves functional minimality and same-object exhaustion. Exact realization requires preservation of original observations through the encoding fibres.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies a kernel necessity argument and a representation-faithfulness criterion. Downstream September papers cite version 49, rather than the preferred 26 September PDF.

#### Scope and limits

The functional roles are not an optional overlay. Agreement under complete queries requires independent individual warrants. Unique or absent outcomes are not a blanket assertion about all research or every question; semantic absence is not computational timeout.

#### Evidence

- [Proposition 2.4, PDF pp. 14–17](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=14)
- [Theorem 2.8 / Corollary 2.9, PDF pp. 20–21](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=20)
- [Theorem 3.1 / Theorem 3.6, PDF pp. 24–27](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=24)
- [Sections 6.2-6.5, PDF pp. 35–37](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=35)
- [Theorem 7.1 / Section 7.1, PDF pp. 41–43](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=41)

### The AMetric Boundary as a Unique Regime-Invariant Constraint on Admissibility-Bearing Construction

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/the-ametric-boundary-18603144/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22848051) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18603144)

Edition: Reference edition; manuscript cover 2026-09-20; publisher release 2026-09-19; 67 PDF pages; 676133 bytes. SHA256: `fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. The AMetric Boundary as a Unique Regime-Invariant Constraint on Admissibility-Bearing Construction: Pre-fixational authority, non-transmissivity, and complete interfaces. Reference edition, 2026-09-20. SHA256 fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22848051.

#### Imports

Locally uses kernel necessity (version 49 in ref.13). The Structure comparison in ref.18 is not a logical back-edge from Structure into the boundary theorem.

#### Establishes

At a fixed authoritative equality-only atom interface, invariant readouts cannot recover additional distinctions without warranted richer input. Theorem 7.5 states the construction-neutral exclusion package with explicit accommodation of independently warranted enrichment.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies the conditional boundary/exclusion result and export discipline. Metricity applies a boundary package to physical metric licensing; the exact AMetric edition imported by the May Metricity paper is unresolved.

#### Scope and limits

Formal symbols, carriers, equality patterns and tuple relations are available before target-specific physical standing. Proposition 3.8 allows invariant formal structures (including equality-based discrete metrics). Theorem 7.5 permits independently warranted richer inputs; it does not rule out every formal distinction, all metric calculations or all research programs.

#### Evidence

- [Section 3.1 / Proposition 3.3 / Definition 3.4, PDF pp. 17–19](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=17)
- [Proposition 3.8, PDF pp. 21–22](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=21)
- [Theorem 7.5 / Section 7.6, PDF pp. 39–40](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=39)

### The Structure of Admissibility

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/the-structure-of-admissibility-10-5281-zenodo-19198249/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22874934) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19198249)

Edition: Publication reference; manuscript cover 2026-09-21; publisher release 2026-09-21; 46 PDF pages; 612137 bytes. SHA256: `065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. The Structure of Admissibility: Bivalent Qualification, Exhaustion, and the Unique Admissible Interior. Publication reference, 2026-09-21. SHA256 065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22874934.

#### Imports

Reconstructs kernel version 49 and AMetric boundary arguments locally; §1.4 distinguishes this support from using later conclusions as premises.

#### Establishes

Bivalent qualification is an exact quotient only when all required original observations are constant on the bit fibres. It constructs the greatest safe interior relative to independently fixed qualification and continuation edges, and gives finite failed-path and exhaustion witnesses.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies complete-profile and continuation-interior machinery used in fixed-domain exhaustion and referenced by ATS. The downstream cited edition is the 20 September examples reference.

#### Scope and limits

The interior may be empty. Uniqueness concerns the complete/maximal interior for fixed data, not every safe subset or a unique physical occupant. Failure retention and negative endpoint absorption have different conditions.

### A Fixed-Domain Exhaustion Theorem

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/a-fixed-domain-exhaustion-theorem-10-5281-zenodo-18682423/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22875070) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18682423)

Edition: Publication reference; manuscript cover 2026-09-21; publisher release 2026-09-21; 39 PDF pages; 574789 bytes. SHA256: `d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. A Fixed-Domain Exhaustion Theorem: Standing, Consequence, and Compositional Closure. Publication reference, 2026-09-21. SHA256 d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22875070.

#### Imports

Reuses the 20 September Structure profile/interior results with short local proofs. Ref.6 names kernel v49; ref.7 names AMetric editorial reference. ATS is a comparison and is explicitly not assumed.

#### Establishes

Adds compositional coverage and joint-constructor descent to complete semantic profiles; exhausts specified failure-witness families under typed boundary discipline. Separates original obligation coverage, closure and candidate identification.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies the finite-use compositional foundation and candidate readout criterion imported by ATS. ATS cites the 20 September composition reference rather than this preferred 21 September publication reference.

#### Scope and limits

Arbitrary semantic coordinates are not automatically a finite implementation. Candidate-set constant readout, single occupant, and unique decomposition are separate results with separate assumptions. Retaining a failure history does not itself force every later endpoint negative; the edge 0-to-0 condition is additional.

### Anchor, Tensor, and Skin

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/anchor-tensor-and-skin-a-fixed-domain-decomposition-theorem-for-admissible-description/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22875011) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18678041)

Edition: Publication reference; manuscript cover 2026-09-21; publisher release 2026-09-21; 36 PDF pages; 538301 bytes. SHA256: `1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. Anchor, Tensor, and Skin: A Fixed-Domain Decomposition Theorem for Admissible Description. Publication reference, 2026-09-21. SHA256 1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22875011.

#### Imports

States a one-way order: Kernel, AMetric, Structure, fixed-domain exhaustion, then ATS. References name kernel v49, AMetric editorial reference, Structure examples reference 20 September and Exhaustion composition reference 20 September.

#### Establishes

Decomposes a fixed-domain admissible description into context (Anchor), complete semantic content (Tensor) and identity-preserving realization (Skin), with reconstruction maps; characterizes minimal realization uniqueness up to commuting bijection and finite-use envelopes/substitution.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies a typed organization for assembling/checking admissible descriptions and certificates. It does not serve as a premise for the earlier general exhaustion theorem.

#### Scope and limits

A complete semantic profile is not merely an admissibility bit and need not identify a unique occupant. Minimal-realization uniqueness does not imply uniqueness among every adequate realization. Sequential substitution requires joint original-domain factorization; a licence alone is not execution.

### Metricity as Licensed Description

[Canonical work page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/metricity-as-licensed-description-10-5281-zenodo-20338474/) | [Edition page](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/) | [Authoritative PDF](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf) | [Exact release DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20338475) | [All-versions work DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20338474)

Edition: May 2026 manuscript; manuscript cover 2026-05; publisher release 2026-05-22; 45 PDF pages; 534152 bytes. SHA256: `6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e`.

Citation: Amos Jay Maley. Metricity as Licensed Description: The L-Metric Boundary and the Realized Physical Interior. May 2026 manuscript, 2026-05. SHA256 6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20338475.

#### Imports

Names Kernel, Structure, AMetric and ATS companions without edition-identifying hashes/dates. Its AMetric exclusion package is a premise of conditional licensing; new September editions must not be silently assigned as the May paper’s imports.

#### Establishes

Distinguishes weak formal/model/calculational interpretation from strong physical interpretation, defines the local L-metric projection, and gives conditional licensing for physical metric description.

#### Supplies downstream

Supplies the distinction between a metric expression and warranted physical relata, records, calibration and interpretation; it offers a licensing branch, rather than an additional premise in the fixed-domain decomposition spine.

#### Scope and limits

Definitions 2.7-2.11 permit weak formal interpretation before physical standing. Corollary 6.3 says licensing does not generate metric structure, standing or ontology. The projection order is a dependency order, not a temporal sequence, and no globally unique metric interface is claimed.

## Uniqueness, absence and implementation scope

Keep complete-profile equivalence, greatest safe interior, constant candidate readout, single occupant and minimal-realization uniqueness separate. Each has different fixed data and hypotheses. A complete profile can leave multiple occupants; a constant consequence need not identify a single quotient input. Evidence: [structure: Theorems 5.5-5.6 / Theorems 6.3-6.6, PDF pp. 16-21; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22874934](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/structure/sha256-065979305b2fc1593abb343e72a86d0ed9c967c089d1a9cbf91be650de25eff2/manuscript.pdf#page=16); [exhaustion: Theorem 8.1 / Corollary 8.2 / Proposition 8.4, PDF pp. 26-27; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875070](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/manuscript.pdf#page=26); [ats: Theorem 3.3, PDF pp. 7-8; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875011](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ats/sha256-1624eacd530dcdaaedec184414c8a7eab8d5096805aee9ffa5452b6f51638c7b/manuscript.pdf#page=7).

Minimal realization uniqueness does not imply uniqueness among every adequate realization. A semantic exhaustion result is not by itself a finite implementation or timeout certificate. Original obligation coverage, compositional closure and candidate identification are separate. Evidence: [exhaustion: Theorem 4.3 / Theorem 4.8, PDF pp. 13-16; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875070](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/manuscript.pdf#page=13); [exhaustion: Theorem 5.9, PDF pp. 21-22; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22875070](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/exhaustion/sha256-d06d39b381edddaafe899f20769b0ba551802b23d7b83121530ecab346feece0/manuscript.pdf#page=21); [kernel: Theorem 7.1 / Section 7.1, PDF pp. 41-43; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=41). None of these source-relative claims establishes global uniqueness over other research programs.

## Access and fidelity

For a question: choose the canonical work page; locate the exact reading PDF and release DOI; inspect the cited definition/theorem with its hypotheses; distinguish any consumer's named imported edition; report unresolved identity instead of inventing a source lock. Catalogue metadata is discovery information, not evidence that every paper has been substantively reviewed.

The six Markdown files linked in [llms.txt](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/llms.txt) are summaries. Full searchable HTML/Markdown manuscript fidelity remains unverified and deferred: equations, proof text, numbering, references and section anchors have not been certified as complete conversions. Do not quote a summary as if it were manuscript proof text. Use the PDFs for those tasks. SHA256 checks and link/page checks are mechanical checks, not independent verification of mathematical claims.
